chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Dawud ibn Kathir al-Raqqi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Are the Sunnahs of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) like the Obligations of Allah (Exalted and Mighty) imposed obligatory obligations upon the servants. So whoever leaves an obligation from the obligatory ones, does not act upon it, and denies it, he is a disbeliever. And the Messenger of Allah commanded matters, all of them being good deeds. So whoever leaves some of what Allah (Exalted and Mighty) commanded His servants to do from the obedience, is not a disbeliever, but he is one who leaves the virtue, deficient in goodness.

key_terms.سُنَنُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between neglecting an obligatory act and a recommended act in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the theological distinction between major disbelief (kufr) and minor deficiency (nuqsan) by differentiating between obligatory duties (fara'id) and recommended acts (sunnah). Neglecting an obligation while denying its status constitutes kufr, whereas omitting a recommended act results only in a loss of extra virtue, preserving the individual's faith. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for understanding the gradations of sin and the criteria for excommunication or maintaining one's status as a believer.
